1	# RL Lab — Architecture
2	
3	**Status:** Approved · **Shape:** Single package · **Last updated:** 2026-10-18 · **Spec:** [spec.md](spec.md)
4	
5	Single package (`rllab`): one learner, one laptop, one install, nothing deployed. The one seam that could become its own package is `refcheck`, the only component that carries Stable-Baselines3 and Gymnasium. It sits behind an optional `check` extra, so a split would move it out as it is.
6	
7	## Overview
8	Every world implements one multi-agent `World` protocol (AD-04): it resets from a seed, steps on one action array for all agents, and reports per-team scores and a drawable state. `train` drives a hand-written learner per team (AD-03) over a world for a fixed step budget. It plays held-out evaluation episodes through `core.play_episode` and writes everything to a run folder through `runlog` (AD-06). `evaluate` replays final checkpoints and both baselines on the final seeds and runs the paired permutation test. `charts` draws learning curves from run folders. `replay` re-simulates any checkpoint or baseline from a seed into a `Trace`, then shows it in a pygame window or writes it to MP4 (AD-07). `refcheck` trains Stable-Baselines3 on the same world through an adapter, kept away from every training run (AD-08).
9	
10	```mermaid
11	flowchart LR
12	  cli --> train & evaluate & charts & replay & refcheck & notes
13	  train --> methods & runlog & worlds & baselines
14	  evaluate --> methods & runlog & worlds & baselines
15	  replay --> methods & runlog & worlds & baselines
16	  refcheck --> evaluate & train & worlds
17	  charts --> runlog & evaluate & baselines
18	  methods --> runlog
19	  worlds & baselines & methods & runlog --> core
20	```
21	
22	## Tech stack
23	| Area | Choice | Decision |
24	|---|---|---|
25	| Language, env | Python 3.12, uv, one `pyproject.toml` | AD-01 |
26	| Networks, autograd | PyTorch ≥ 2.5, CPU wheels; `nn` layers and `optim` only | AD-02 |
27	| Numerics, world physics | NumPy ≥ 2.1, vectorised over agents | AD-04 |
28	| Learning methods | Hand-written DQN (discrete) and PPO (continuous), one learner per team | AD-03 |
29	| Seeds, parallel runs | `np.random.SeedSequence`, one spawned process per run | AD-05 |
30	| Run storage | JSON record + JSON Lines logs + `torch.save` checkpoints per run folder | AD-06 |
31	| Replay window, video | pygame-ce ≥ 2.5; imageio ≥ 2.36 with imageio-ffmpeg ≥ 0.5 (bundled ffmpeg) | AD-07 |
32	| Charts | matplotlib ≥ 3.9, PNG + SVG | — |
33	| Reference check | stable-baselines3 ≥ 2.4 + gymnasium ≥ 1.0, optional extra `check` | AD-08 |
34	| Settings | TOML files in `configs/`, read with `tomllib` into frozen dataclasses owned by `core` | AD-12 |
35	| CLI | `argparse`, one `rllab` console script | — |
36	| Tests, import rules | pytest; import-linter | — |
37	
38	## Components
39	| Component | Responsibility | Covers | Depends on |
40	|---|---|---|---|
41	| `core` | World and policy protocols, shared types (run and method settings included, AD-12), held-out seed sets, and the one episode loop every other component plays through | WORLD-01–WORLD-07 (interface), WORLD edge cases | — |
42	| `worlds` | Snake, the three fish-tank variants, predator-prey and the two check worlds, behind `worlds.make` | SNAKE-01–SNAKE-06, FISH-01–FISH-08, PREY-01–PREY-06, TRAIN-06 (check worlds) | `core` |
43	| `baselines` | Random play for any action format, each world's hand-written rule acting on observations only, and their mean scores on the evaluation seeds | EVAL-01, EVAL-02, SNAKE-07, FISH-09, PREY-07 | `core`, `worlds` |
44	| `methods` | Hand-written DQN and PPO learners behind `Learner`; rebuilds a frozen `Policy` from a checkpoint | CHECK-01, TRAIN-07 | `core`, `runlog` |
45	| `train` | One run over the step budget: per-team learners, checkpoints, in-training evaluations, invalid-number stop; batches across cores; the check-world gate | TRAIN-01–TRAIN-07, QR-01–QR-03, TRAIN edge cases | `core`, `worlds`, `baselines`, `methods`, `runlog` |
46	| `runlog` | Run folders: record, episode and evaluation logs, checkpoints, live progress, run lookup | LOG-01, LOG-02, LOG-06, TRAIN-03 (storage), TRAIN edge cases (overwrite, incomplete) | `core` |
47	| `charts` | Learning curves with range bands and baseline lines, extra measures, two-team curves, pairing heatmaps; follows the `dataviz` skill | LOG-03–LOG-05, PREY-10, PREY-09 (chart), LOG edge cases | `core`, `baselines`, `runlog`, `evaluate` |
48	| `evaluate` | Final evaluation on the final seeds, paired permutation tests run with the `null-hypothesis-testing` skill, verdicts, summaries, fixed-opponent team evaluation, pairing grids, collapse flags | EVAL-03–EVAL-06, SNAKE-08, FISH-10, PREY-08, PREY-09, QR-05, EVAL and PREY edge cases | `core`, `worlds`, `baselines`, `methods`, `runlog` |
49	| `replay` | Opens replay sides, re-simulates checkpoints or baselines into a `Trace`; pygame viewer with pause, step, speeds, side by side and sight overlay, testable headless; MP4 export | REPLAY-01–REPLAY-08, QR-04, REPLAY edge cases | `core`, `worlds`, `baselines`, `methods`, `runlog` |
50	| `refcheck` | Trains and evaluates Stable-Baselines3 DQN/PPO on a world through a Gymnasium/VecEnv adapter, and compares with the hand-written summary | CHECK-02, CHECK-03, CHECK edge case | `core`, `worlds`, `train`, `evaluate`, `runlog` |
51	| `notes` | Write-up scaffold with the three headings only, and the finish check (parts present, struggle link, broken links) | NOTES-01–NOTES-03, NOTES edge case | — |
52	| `cli` | The `rllab` command: dispatches each trigger to its pipeline entry and prints the result; owns no step (AD-10) | LOG-06 (view), REPLAY-01 (entry) | `core`, `worlds`, `baselines`, `methods`, `train`, `runlog`, `charts`, `evaluate`, `replay`, `refcheck`, `notes` |
53	
54	## Interfaces
55	See [packages/rllab/contract.md](packages/rllab/contract.md).
56	
57	## Data
58	No external datasets: every world is simulated. Generated data lives under `runs/<world>/<variant>/<run-name>/` (AD-06):
59	- `run.json`: the LOG-01 record, the run's config and its status (`running`, `finished`, `incomplete`, `failed` with step and value).
60	- `episodes.jsonl`: one line per training episode (LOG-02). `evals.jsonl`: one line per 5% evaluation point (TRAIN-04), flushed as written so `rllab watch` reads it live (LOG-06).
61	- `checkpoints/ckpt_<pct>.pt`: 11 checkpoints, every 10% (TRAIN-03), each holding the `WorldSpec`, per-team method configs and state dicts.
62	- Final evaluations under `runs/<world>/<variant>/_eval/<date>/` (`summary.json`, per-episode scores), reference runs under `_reference/`, charts and videos under `reports/<world>/`, write-ups at `notes/<world>.md`.
63	
64	Seeds come from three disjoint ranges (AD-05): training episode seeds drawn by the run's generator from [0, 10⁶), the 20 in-training evaluation seeds 1,000,000–1,000,019, and the 100 final seeds 2,000,000–2,000,099, shared by every run and baseline.
65	
66	## Cross-cutting concerns
67	- **Determinism (WORLD-02, TRAIN-02, REPLAY-02, FISH-11, PREY-11):** no global random state. Each episode seed spawns the world's and the policies' generators, and torch runs single-threaded with deterministic algorithms (AD-05). A committed digest of a short snake run's logs and final checkpoint is checked in CI. A later world that changes it fails the build (FISH-11, PREY-11), and so does a fish digest once S2 lands.
68	- **No outside RL code in training (CHECK-01):** import-linter forbids `stable_baselines3` and `gymnasium` outside `refcheck`, and a test asserts neither is in `sys.modules` after a training run (AD-08).
69	- **Speed (QR-01, QR-02, QR-04, QR-05):** world physics is NumPy over all agents at once, learners batch every team's observations into one forward pass, and evaluation spreads seeds over processes. `rllab` logs each run's wall time against the 60-minute budget, and a timing test plays a 1,000-step replay headless.
70	- **GPU (QR-03):** `device` is a run setting, `cpu` by default; a rented GPU run uses the same code, and its cost goes in the write-up by hand.
71	- **Offline (QR-06):** nothing imports a network client. ffmpeg comes bundled with imageio-ffmpeg, and fonts come from pygame's built-in one.
72	- **Outputs:** every step that writes a chart, video or write-up returns a `core.Output` naming the file and what it was made from, so a write-up can cite it (NOTES-02).
73	- **Errors:** bad actions raise `core.ActionError` naming the agent and value (never clipped). Spec mismatches on checkpoint load raise `methods.SpecMismatchError` naming the field. Mixed-settings charts raise `charts.MixedRunsError` naming the differing settings.
74	- **Skills:** `charts` follows `dataviz` for every chart (LOG-04). `evaluate.compare` is built and checked with `null-hypothesis-testing`, whose inputs are its signature (EVAL-04).
75	
76	## Project layout
77	```
78	src/rllab/     → core/ worlds/ baselines/ methods/ train/ runlog/ charts/ evaluate/ replay/ refcheck/ notes/ cli/ — one folder per component; __init__ exports its contract
79	                 train/pipelines/ holds the PL-01–PL-03 entries, cli/pipelines/ the PL-04–PL-12 entries (AD-10)
80	configs/       → one TOML per world and variant: budget, per-team method settings
81	runs/          → generated run folders (git-ignored)
82	reports/       → charts and videos kept alongside the write-ups
83	notes/         → one write-up per world, the learner's own words
84	tests/         → folders only; files are planned in pipelines.md
85	```
86	
87	## Decisions
88	### AD-01: Python 3.12 in one uv-managed package
89	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** system
90	- **Context:** One learner on an Apple Silicon laptop; PyTorch, pygame-ce and Stable-Baselines3 all ship arm64 macOS wheels for Python. QR-06 needs the whole install to work offline once set up.
91	- **Decision:** Python 3.12, one `rllab` package with a `uv.lock`. Stable-Baselines3 and Gymnasium go in an optional `check` extra.
92	- **Alternatives:** Python 3.13: wheels for some libraries lag. Separate `rllab-check` package: a real boundary only if the reference stack becomes a burden, so it is a named seam for now.
93	- **Consequences:** `requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"`. Training can run without the `check` extra installed, which proves CHECK-01 at install level too.
94	
95	### AD-02: PyTorch for networks and gradients, not for the learning algorithm
96	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** system
97	- **Context:** CHECK-01 allows automatic gradient computation but the learner writes action choice, learning targets and updates. Networks are small MLPs on observations of tens of numbers (WORLD-03). Training is CPU-only (QR-01).
98	- **Decision:** Learners use `torch.nn` layers, `torch.optim` optimisers and autograd. Replay buffers, exploration, targets, advantage estimation, clipping and update schedules are hand-written in `methods`.
99	- **Alternatives:** NumPy with hand-derived backprop: teaches backprop, which is not this project's subject, and is slower to debug. JAX: capable, but less familiar CPU tooling and a functional style that hides the update loop.
100	- **Consequences:** `torch.set_num_threads(1)` per run process (AD-05); small batches stay fast on CPU. The PyTorch install is about 200 MB.
101	
102	### AD-03: DQN for discrete actions, PPO for continuous ones, one learner per team
103	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** system
104	- **Context:** Snake has 3 discrete actions (SNAKE-02); fish and predator-prey push with two numbers in [−1, 1] (FISH-02, PREY-02). Many-fish has 8 agents (FISH-06), and predator-prey has two teams learning at once (TRAIN-07). The brief wants each world to teach one idea, and wants checking against a reference implementation (CHECK-02).
105	- **Decision:** `dqn` (replay buffer, target network, ε-greedy, Huber loss) for snake and the discrete check world. `ppo` (Gaussian policy, GAE, clipped objective) for fish, predator-prey and the continuous check world. All agents of a team share one learner (parameter sharing over a batch of agents). Teams have separate learners in the same run. Evaluation and replay act deterministically: greedy for DQN, the mean action for PPO.
106	- **Alternatives:** PPO everywhere: one method fewer, but snake would not teach value learning. SAC for fish: strong on continuous control, but a third method and harder to explain for many agents. Tabular Q-learning for snake: SNAKE-06 includes length, an unbounded number, so the table would need discretising.
107	- **Consequences:** Two methods to write, each with a check world (TRAIN-06) and a Stable-Baselines3 equivalent (AD-08). A prey that leaves the episode is masked out of its team's batch.
108	
109	### AD-04: Our own multi-agent World protocol, not Gymnasium or PettingZoo
110	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** system
111	- **Context:** WORLD-01–WORLD-07 need seeded resets, a declared spec, team-labelled agents, per-team scores with a direction, and a drawable state. The brief bets that one core serves a grid game, smooth movement and two teams.
112	- **Decision:** `core.World` is a small protocol. Observations, actions, rewards and active masks are NumPy arrays indexed by agent, teams map to agent indices in `WorldSpec`, and `draw()` returns a `DrawState`. "Not seen" entries are a 0/1 flag followed by zeros, so lengths stay fixed (WORLD-03, FISH-07, PREY-06).
113	- **Alternatives:** Gymnasium: single-agent, with no teams, score direction or drawable state, so all of those would be extras. PettingZoo parallel API: multi-agent, but dict-per-agent stepping is slow in Python and adds a dependency the learner didn't write.
114	- **Consequences:** `refcheck` writes the one Gymnasium/VecEnv adapter (AD-08). Every world implements all five methods, and `core.play_episode` is the only episode loop.
115	
116	### AD-05: Seeds from SeedSequence, disjoint held-out ranges, one process per run
117	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** system
118	- **Context:** WORLD-01, WORLD-02, TRAIN-02 and REPLAY-02 need exact repeats; TRAIN-04 and EVAL-03 need seeds never used in training; TRAIN-05 and QR-02 need runs in parallel, one per core.
119	- **Decision:** A run seed spawns the learner's, exploration and episode-seed generators through `np.random.SeedSequence`. An episode seed spawns the world's and the policies' generators inside `core.play_episode`. Training draws episode seeds from [0, 10⁶); evaluation seeds are the fixed `core.EVAL_SEEDS` and `core.FINAL_SEEDS` ranges (see Data). `train.run_batch` runs each config in its own `spawn` process with `torch.set_num_threads(1)` and `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`.
120	- **Alternatives:** Global `np.random.seed`/`torch.manual_seed`: order-dependent, breaks once evaluation interleaves with training. Threads: the GIL serialises the Python world loop.
121	- **Consequences:** Identical runs are promised on the same machine only (TRAIN-02). In-training evaluation never touches the training generators, so turning evaluation off for a test leaves training identical.
122	
123	### AD-06: Run folders of JSON, JSON Lines and torch checkpoints
124	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** system
125	- **Context:** LOG-01 and LOG-02 need a record and per-episode logs. LOG-06 needs them readable while the run writes, at most one evaluation point behind. A stopped run keeps its checkpoints and is marked incomplete. A run name that already exists is refused (TRAIN edge cases). REPLAY edge cases need a checkpoint to carry its world spec.
126	- **Decision:** One folder per run (see Data). Logs are append-only JSON Lines, flushed at every evaluation point; `run.json` is rewritten atomically (write, then rename) on each status change. A checkpoint is a `torch.save` dict of spec, method configs and state dicts, loaded with `weights_only=True`.
127	- **Alternatives:** Parquet: fast to read but not appendable while a run is live. SQLite: one file for everything, but concurrent writers from parallel runs need care and the files are no longer readable by eye.
128	- **Consequences:** Charts and evaluation read whole JSONL files; at ~10⁴ episodes per run that is instant. A crashed process leaves `run.json` at `running`; `runlog` reports any `running` run with no live process as incomplete.
129	
130	### AD-07: Replays re-simulate into a Trace, shown with pygame-ce and saved with imageio-ffmpeg
131	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** system
132	- **Context:** REPLAY-01–REPLAY-08 need any checkpoint or baseline from any seed, step back, 4 speeds, side by side, a sight overlay and video export. QR-04 needs ≥ 30 steps/s; QR-06 needs it offline. Worlds are deterministic (AD-05), so nothing needs recording during training.
133	- **Decision:** `replay.trace_sides` (or, for one side, `to_trace` over a traced `core.play_episode`) plays the whole episode headless through `core.play_episode` into a `Trace` of frames (at most the world's `max_steps`), then the viewer only draws frames. Stepping back is an index change. 1× is 30 steps/s. pygame-ce draws circles, cells and text; MP4 (H.264) export goes through imageio's ffmpeg writer.
134	- **Alternatives:** matplotlib animation: slow at 16× for 8 fish and clumsy keyboard control. A browser viewer: smooth, but a local web server and JavaScript stack for one user (spec: everything local).
135	- **Consequences:** The `Trace` is testable without a window, so REPLAY-02 is a frame comparison. Memory is one episode of `DrawState`s, under 1,000 frames of a few dozen objects.
136	
137	### AD-08: Stable-Baselines3 as the reference, isolated in `refcheck`
138	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** system
139	- **Context:** CHECK-02 needs an established implementation of the same kind of method (DQN, PPO; AD-03) trained on the same world, budget and seeds; CHECK-01 forbids it inside training runs. Worlds speak `core.World`, not Gymnasium (AD-04).
140	- **Decision:** `refcheck` wraps a world as a Gymnasium env (single agent) or as an SB3 `VecEnv` with one slot per agent of the learning team (many-fish: 8 slots stepping one world, matching parameter sharing). It trains SB3 `DQN` or `PPO` for 5 seeds and evaluates on `core.FINAL_SEEDS` through `core.play_episode`. In predator-prey, SB3 cannot co-train two models, so each team's reference trains against the rule-based opponent, the same opponent PREY-08 evaluates against.
141	- **Alternatives:** CleanRL single-file scripts: easy to read, but they would need editing to fit our worlds, which weakens them as a reference. RLlib: multi-agent native, but a heavy distributed stack for a laptop.
142	- **Consequences:** SB3's default hyperparameters differ from ours; `refcheck` starts from the hand-written method's settings where SB3 has the same knob. The predator-prey reference answers a narrower question than co-training, so CHECK-03's 80% bar compares a fixed-opponent reference with a co-trained team there; the learner accepted this (2026-10-17).
143	
144	### AD-09: Every batch first runs the method's check world
145	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** system
146	- **Context:** TRAIN-06 needs every learning method to learn a hand-derived best behaviour before it is used in a world. Bugs in RL are silent (brief), and methods change while a world is built.
147	- **Decision:** `train.run_check` trains each team method in a config on its check world: for DQN a 6-state corridor with two exits, left of state 0 (reward 0.8) and right of state 5 (reward 1.0), γ = 0.9, so the best action is left in states 0–1 and right in 2–5 and a learner biased to one action can't pass; for PPO a 1-D point that is rewarded for reaching a target, where the best push is the sign of the offset. It needs ≥ 95% agreement over every check-world state. `train.run_batch` runs the same check steps with the batch's method settings before starting any run and refuses the batch on failure. `rllab check <config>` runs it alone.
148	- **Alternatives:** A recorded pass per method version: saves seconds but goes stale silently when code changes. A test only: passes in CI but not for the settings actually used.
149	- **Consequences:** Each batch spends under a minute on the check. A check-world settings override exists because a world's tuned settings (e.g. buffer size) may be too large for a 6-state world.
150	
151	### AD-10: Pipeline entries are the public API; `cli` only dispatches
152	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** system
153	- **Context:** Pipeline design gave every workflow one entry function calling named steps (PL-01–PL-12). Entries import their steps' owners, so where an entry lives sets an import direction. PL-03 runs PL-02 in worker processes, so `train` can't depend on `cli`. A chart, a summary and a heatmap each need two or more components that the `cli` row already depends on.
154	- **Decision:** `train` hosts the PL-01–PL-03 entries (`run_check`, `run_train`, `run_batch`) and exports them as its contract. Every other entry lives in `cli/pipelines/`. Entries return contract types. `cli/__main__.py` parses arguments, loads configs through `train.load_run_configs`, calls the entry, prints its result and sets the exit code; `cli` owns no pipeline step.
155	- **Alternatives:** All entries in `cli`: the batch's worker processes would import `cli`, inverting the dependency. Each entry in its main component: `charts` and `evaluate` entries would need `runlog` and `baselines` steps, which they may do, but the replay and refcheck entries would need printing in their own components.
156	- **Consequences:** The contract carries the train entries, the config loader and every step function a `cli` entry calls. `cli` has no step tests; its intent tests drive `main` with arguments.
157	
158	### AD-11: Stay a single package past the size triggers
159	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** system
160	- **Context:** The contract passed its 200-line size ceiling and the package has 12 pipelines, past the ~3-pipeline Grow trigger. The learner chose to stay single (2026-10-17). Nothing runs or deploys on its own, and the one dependency stack the rest shouldn't carry (Stable-Baselines3, Gymnasium) is already isolated as the optional `check` extra in `refcheck` (AD-08).
161	- **Decision:** `rllab` stays one package. Size is handled by `dt context`, which loads only the contract sections and pipelines a task reads, and import-linter keeps the component directions.
162	- **Alternatives:** Split `refcheck` into its own package: a real boundary, but already met by the extra. Split the shared core from the worlds: every world needs the core, and the core has no other consumer.
163	- **Consequences:** The Grow triggers stay reported by `dt` and are answered by this decision. A new trigger (a part that runs on its own, a heavy new stack) reopens it.
164	
165	### AD-12: Run and method settings types live in `core`
166	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-18 · **Scope:** system
167	- **Context:** The M1 interface task found that `runlog.RunRecord`, `runlog.RunWriter` and `runlog.Checkpoint` hold a run's config and per-team method configs (LOG-01, AD-06), whose types `train` and `methods` owned. `runlog` may import only `core`, and import-linter counts `TYPE_CHECKING` imports too, so no version of those types could be written.
168	- **Decision:** A type that a lower component stores but a higher one fills lives in `core`. `RunConfig`, `MethodConfig` and the `Settings` alias are `core` types. `methods` still declares each method's keys and defaults, and `train.load_run_configs` still builds and fills the configs; neither owns the types.
169	- **Alternatives:** Move `RunRecord`, `Checkpoint` and `RunWriter` up into `train`: `methods`, `evaluate`, `replay` and `charts` read checkpoints and records, so they would all depend on `train`, and the batch's worker processes would import them. Store the config in `runlog` as an untyped mapping: loses the frozen type at every reader.
170	- **Consequences:** `runlog` keeps `core` as its only dependency, and the import layers are unchanged. Every consumer imports `RunConfig` and `MethodConfig` from `core`.
171	
172	## Risks and open questions
173	- **Many-fish and predator-prey speed (QR-01, QR-02).** 8–10 agents, 1,000-step episodes and 21 × 20 evaluation episodes may not fit 60 minutes in Python. Mitigation: NumPy physics over all agents, evaluation in a worker process, and a timing check in the first fish build; QR-03's GPU route doesn't help a CPU-bound world loop.
174	- **5 parallel runs on mixed cores (QR-02).** Apple Silicon's efficiency cores run slower; 5 runs may not all land on performance cores. Measured in the first snake batch.
175

180	| 2026-10-17 | Pipeline entries as public API; contract changes routed from pipeline design | pipeline-design | AD-10 |
181	| 2026-10-17 | Stay single package past the size triggers | learner's decision | AD-11 |
182	| 2026-10-17 | 11 checkpoints and an 11 × 11 pairing grid; two-exit DQN check corridor (AD-09) | routed from test-planning | TRAIN-03, PREY-09 (changed) |
183	| 2026-10-18 | Run and method settings types move to `core`; `charts` depends on `baselines` | M1-T01 contract-change escalation | AD-12 |

33:- **WORLD-01** A world starts a new episode from a seed, and the same seed always gives the same starting state.
35:- **WORLD-02** Given the same seed and the same sequence of actions, a world produces the same sequence of observations, rewards and end signals.
37:- **WORLD-03** Each agent's observation is a fixed-length list of numbers, never an image.
39:- **WORLD-04** A world declares its agents, the observation length and the action format (a choice from a fixed set, or a list of numbers within stated limits) before any episode starts.
41:- **WORLD-05** Every world reports a per-episode score with a stated direction (higher is better, or lower is better), used by evaluation and charts.
43:- **WORLD-06** A world reports its drawable state at every step (positions, sizes and kinds of every object) for the replay viewer.
45:- **WORLD-07** A world can hold more than one agent, each agent belonging to a named team.
58:- **TRAIN-01** A training run is started from a world, a variant, the method's settings and a seed, and runs for a stated budget of environment steps.
60:- **TRAIN-02** The same world, settings and seed on the same machine give an identical training run.
62:- **TRAIN-03** A run saves a checkpoint at every 10% of its budget, from the start (untrained) to the end.
64:- **TRAIN-04** A run evaluates its current agent at every 5% of its budget on 20 episodes whose seeds are never used in training.
66:- **TRAIN-05** Several runs of the same world with different seeds can be started together, one per processor core.
68:- **TRAIN-06** Every learning method, before it is used in a world, learns the known best behavior in a tiny check world whose best behavior is worked out by hand.
70:- **TRAIN-07** In worlds with more than one team, each team has its own learning method and settings, and all teams learn during the same run.
84:- **LOG-01** Every run records its world, variant, method settings, seed, budget, start and end times, and whether it finished.
86:- **LOG-02** Every run logs, for each training episode, the episode's score, length and total reward per team.
88:- **LOG-03** For a world and variant with at least 3 finished runs, a learning-curve chart shows evaluation score against environment steps: the mean across runs as a line, the lowest-to-highest range across runs as a band, and each baseline's mean score as a horizontal reference line.
90:- **LOG-04** Learning-curve charts follow the `dataviz` skill's guidance for form, colour and labelling.
92:- **LOG-05** Each world can add its own logged measures (e.g. snake length at death, hits per fish), which are charted the same way as the score.
94:- **LOG-06** The learner can view the latest logged values of a run while it trains.
143:- **EVAL-05** "Clearly beats" also needs every single run to beat the rule baseline: each run's final mean score is better than the rule-based baseline's mean score.
145:- **EVAL-06** Final evaluation produces one summary per world and variant: mean and range of learned scores across runs, both baseline means, the EVAL-04 test results and the EVAL-05 verdict.
190:- **SNAKE-01** The world is a 10 × 10 grid with one snake starting 3 cells long in the middle, and one food item on a random free cell.
192:- **SNAKE-02** Each step the snake chooses one of three actions: turn left, turn right or go straight.
194:- **SNAKE-03** Eating food grows the snake by one cell, adds 1 to the score and places new food on a random free cell.
196:- **SNAKE-04** The episode ends when the head hits a wall or the snake's body, or after 100 steps without eating.
198:- **SNAKE-05** The score is the food eaten in the episode (higher is better).
200:- **SNAKE-06** The snake observes a fixed list of numbers: danger straight ahead, left and right; its heading; the food's direction relative to its head; and its length.
202:- **SNAKE-07** The rule-based baseline moves toward the food along the shorter axis, unless that move would end the episode next step, in which case it takes any move that does not.
204:- **SNAKE-08** The trained snake beats both baselines as in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05.
235:- **FISH-10** Every variant's trained fish beat both baselines as in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05.
264:- **PREY-08** Each trained team is evaluated against fixed opponents: trained prey against the rule-based predators, compared with random and rule-based prey; trained predators against the rule-based prey, compared with random and rule-based predators. Each passes as in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05.

"""Shared types: world and policy protocols, run settings and the held-out seed sets."""

from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, fields
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol, TypeAlias

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

Direction: TypeAlias = Literal["higher", "lower"]
Settings: TypeAlias = Mapping[str, int | float | str | bool]
Array: TypeAlias = npt.NDArray[Any]

EVAL_SEEDS: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(1_000_000, 1_000_020))
FINAL_SEEDS: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(2_000_000, 2_000_100))


def _same(a: object, b: object) -> bool:
    """Field-by-field equality that compares arrays by dtype, shape and values."""
    if isinstance(a, np.ndarray) or isinstance(b, np.ndarray):
        return (
            isinstance(a, np.ndarray)
            and isinstance(b, np.ndarray)
            and a.dtype == b.dtype
            and np.array_equal(a, b)
        )
    return bool(a == b)


def _fields_equal(a: object, b: object) -> bool:
    if type(a) is not type(b):
        return False
    return all(_same(getattr(a, f.name), getattr(b, f.name)) for f in fields(a))  # type: ignore[arg-type]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Discrete:
    n: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Box:
    dims: int
    low: float
    high: float


ActionSpace: TypeAlias = Discrete | Box


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TeamSpec:
    name: str
    agents: tuple[int, ...]
    score_name: str
    direction: Direction


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MeasureSpec:
    name: str
    team: str
    direction: Direction


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WorldSpec:
    world: str
    variant: str
    agents: tuple[str, ...]
    teams: tuple[TeamSpec, ...]
    obs_len: int
    action: ActionSpace
    max_steps: int
    measures: tuple[MeasureSpec, ...]
    sight: float | None


@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class Step:
    obs: Array
    rewards: Array
    active: Array
    done: bool
    truncated: bool

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        return _fields_equal(self, other)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EpisodeResult:
    seed: int
    length: int
    scores: Mapping[str, float]
    team_rewards: Mapping[str, float]
    measures: Mapping[str, float]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Drawable:
    kind: str
    x: float
    y: float
    size: float
    team: str | None
    agent: int | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DrawState:
    width: float
    height: float
    objects: tuple[Drawable, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class Frame:
    step: int
    draw: DrawState
    scores: Mapping[str, float]
    rewards: Array

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        return _fields_equal(self, other)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Episode:
    result: EpisodeResult
    frames: tuple[Frame, ...] | None
    hit_step_limit: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Output:
    path: Path
    kind: Literal["chart", "video", "writeup"]
    made_from: tuple[str, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MethodConfig:
    method: Literal["dqn", "ppo"]
    settings: Settings


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunConfig:
    name: str
    world: str
    variant: str
    methods: Mapping[str, MethodConfig]
    seed: int
    budget: int
    check_settings: Mapping[str, Settings]
    device: str = "cpu"


class ActionError(ValueError):
    """An action outside the world's declared format; never clipped."""

    def __init__(self, agent: str, value: object) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"action {value!r} of agent {agent!r} is outside the action format")
        self.agent = agent
        self.value = value


class World(Protocol):
    spec: WorldSpec

    def reset(self, seed: int) -> Step: ...

    def step(self, actions: Array) -> Step: ...

    def result(self) -> EpisodeResult: ...

    def draw(self) -> DrawState: ...


class Policy(Protocol):
    def act(self, obs: Array, rng: np.random.Generator) -> Array: ...

def _same(a: object, b: object) -> bool:
    """Field-by-field equality that compares arrays by dtype, shape and values."""
    if isinstance(a, np.ndarray) or isinstance(b, np.ndarray):
        return (

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

type Direction = Literal["higher", "lower"]
type Settings = Mapping[str, int | float | str | bool]
type Array = npt.NDArray[Any]

EVAL_SEEDS: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(1_000_000, 1_000_020))
FINAL_SEEDS: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(2_000_000, 2_000_100))


def _same(a: object, b: object) -> bool:
    """Equality that compares arrays by dtype, shape and values."""
    if isinstance(a, np.ndarray) or isinstance(b, np.ndarray):
        return (
            isinstance(a, np.ndarray)
            and isinstance(b, np.ndarray)
            and a.dtype == b.dtype
            and np.array_equal(a, b)
        )
    return bool(a == b)


def _fields_equal(a: object, b: object) -> bool:
    """Field-by-field equality for the frozen types that hold arrays."""
    if type(a) is not type(b):
        return False
    return all(_same(x, y) for x, y in zip(vars(a).values(), vars(b).values(), strict=True))

"""JSON form of the contract types, for contract samples, fixtures and run-folder files.

`to_json` turns a contract value into plain JSON data; `from_json` rebuilds it from the type's
annotations. Arrays are `{"dtype", "shape", "data"}`, paths are strings, datetimes ISO strings,
timedeltas seconds, tuples lists and dataclasses objects keyed by field name.
"""

import json
import types
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import MISSING, fields, is_dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal, TypeAliasType, Union, cast, get_args, get_origin, get_type_hints

import numpy as np

# The boundary fixtures (CR-09): tests/contracts/<id>.<symbol>/ in the project checkout.
CONTRACTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "tests" / "contracts"


def _short(value: np.float32) -> float:
    """The shortest decimal that reads back as the same float32."""
    return float(str(value))


def _array_json(value: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    array = cast(np.ndarray[Any, Any], value)
    if array.dtype == np.float32:
        data = np.vectorize(_short, otypes=[float])(array).tolist()
    else:
        data = array.tolist()
    return {"dtype": str(array.dtype), "shape": list(array.shape), "data": data}


def _mapping_json(value: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {str(k): to_json(v) for k, v in cast(Mapping[Any, Any], value).items()}


def _sequence_json(value: Any) -> list[Any]:
    return [to_json(v) for v in value]


_ENCODERS: tuple[tuple[type[Any] | tuple[type[Any], ...], Callable[[Any], Any]], ...] = (
    (np.ndarray, _array_json),
    (Mapping, _mapping_json),
    ((list, tuple), _sequence_json),
    (Path, lambda p: cast(Path, p).as_posix()),
    (datetime, lambda d: cast(datetime, d).isoformat()),
    (timedelta, lambda d: cast(timedelta, d).total_seconds()),
    (np.generic, lambda g: cast(np.generic, g).item()),
)


def to_json(value: object) -> Any:
    """Plain JSON data (dicts, lists, strings, numbers, booleans, None) for a contract value."""
    if is_dataclass(value) and not isinstance(value, type):
        return {f.name: to_json(getattr(value, f.name)) for f in fields(value)}
    for kinds, encode in _ENCODERS:
        if isinstance(value, kinds):
            return encode(value)
    return value


def _expect(ok: bool, tp: object, data: object) -> None:
    if not ok:
        raise TypeError(f"{data!r} is not a {tp}")


def _decode_int(tp: Any, data: Any) -> int:
    _expect(isinstance(data, int) and not isinstance(data, bool), tp, data)
    return cast(int, data)


def _decode_float(tp: Any, data: Any) -> float:
    _expect(isinstance(data, int | float) and not isinstance(data, bool), tp, data)
    return float(data)


def _decode_exact(tp: Any, data: Any) -> Any:
    _expect(isinstance(data, tp), tp, data)
    return data


def _decode_literal(tp: Any, data: Any) -> Any:
    _expect(data in get_args(tp), tp, data)
    return data


def _decode_union(tp: Any, data: Any) -> Any:
    for option in get_args(tp):
        try:
            return from_json(option, data)
        except (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError):
            continue
    raise TypeError(f"{data!r} matches no member of {tp}")


def _decode_tuple(tp: Any, data: Any) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
    _expect(isinstance(data, list), tp, data)
    args = get_args(tp)
    if len(args) == 2 and args[1] is Ellipsis:
        return tuple(from_json(args[0], item) for item in data)
    _expect(len(args) == len(data), tp, data)
    return tuple(from_json(arg, item) for arg, item in zip(args, data, strict=True))


def _decode_list(tp: Any, data: Any) -> list[Any]:
    _expect(isinstance(data, list), tp, data)
    (item_type,) = get_args(tp) or (Any,)
    return [from_json(item_type, item) for item in data]


def _decode_mapping(tp: Any, data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    _expect(isinstance(data, dict), tp, data)
    _, value_type = get_args(tp) or (str, Any)
    return {str(k): from_json(value_type, v) for k, v in data.items()}


def _decode_array(tp: Any, data: Any) -> np.ndarray[Any, Any]:
    _expect(isinstance(data, dict) and set(data) == {"dtype", "shape", "data"}, tp, data)
    return np.asarray(data["data"], dtype=data["dtype"]).reshape(data["shape"])


def _decode_dataclass(tp: Any, data: Any) -> Any:
    _expect(isinstance(data, dict), tp, data)
    hints = get_type_hints(tp)
    names = {f.name for f in fields(tp)}
    required = {f.name for f in fields(tp) if f.default is MISSING}
    _expect(required <= set(data) <= names, tp, data)
    return tp(**{name: from_json(hints[name], value) for name, value in data.items()})


_DECODERS: dict[Any, Callable[[Any, Any], Any]] = {
    Any: lambda _, data: data,
    object: lambda _, data: data,
    type(None): lambda tp, data: _decode_exact(tp, data),
    bool: _decode_exact,
    str: _decode_exact,
    int: _decode_int,
    float: _decode_float,
    Path: lambda tp, data: Path(_decode_exact(str, data)),
    datetime: lambda tp, data: datetime.fromisoformat(_decode_exact(str, data)),
    timedelta: lambda tp, data: timedelta(seconds=_decode_float(float, data)),
    Literal: _decode_literal,
    Union: _decode_union,
    types.UnionType: _decode_union,
    tuple: _decode_tuple,
    list: _decode_list,
    Sequence: _decode_list,
    dict: _decode_mapping,
    Mapping: _decode_mapping,
    np.ndarray: _decode_array,
}


def from_json(tp: Any, data: Any) -> Any:
    """Rebuild a value of type `tp` from `to_json` output; `TypeError` if the data doesn't fit."""
    if isinstance(tp, TypeAliasType):
        return from_json(tp.__value__, data)
    origin = get_origin(tp) or tp
    decode = _DECODERS.get(origin)
    if decode is None and is_dataclass(origin):
        decode = _decode_dataclass
    if decode is None:
        raise TypeError(f"no JSON form for {tp}")
    return decode(tp, data)


def load_sample[T](tp: type[T], symbol: str, case: str) -> T:
    """The sample `case` of the contract folder `tests/contracts/<symbol>/`, as a `tp`."""
    path = CONTRACTS / symbol / "samples" / f"{case}.json"
    return cast(T, from_json(tp, json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))))

"""Replay doubles of `core.World` and `core.Policy`, and the `core.play_episode` fake.

Each serves a recording from `tests/contracts/<id>.<symbol>/samples/`. A double returns what was
recorded, whatever it is given, and keeps what it was given, so a test can compare the two.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace

import numpy as np

from rllab.core.codec import load_sample
from rllab.core.types import (
    ActionError,
    ActionSpace,
    Array,
    Discrete,
    DrawState,
    Episode,
    EpisodeResult,
    Policy,
    Step,
    World,
    WorldSpec,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RecordedStep:
    """One `World.step` call: the actions given and what the world returned and showed."""

    actions: Array
    step: Step
    draw: DrawState
    result: EpisodeResult


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WorldRecording:
    """A recorded episode: the reset (seed, first step, drawing, tallies) and every step after."""

    spec: WorldSpec
    seed: int
    start: Step
    draw: DrawState
    result: EpisodeResult
    steps: tuple[RecordedStep, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PolicyRecording:
    """Observations a policy was shown and the actions it returned, in order."""

    description: str
    obs: tuple[Array, ...]
    actions: tuple[Array, ...]


def _inside(space: ActionSpace, action: Array) -> bool:
    if isinstance(space, Discrete):
        return (
            action.ndim == 0
            and np.issubdtype(action.dtype, np.integer)
            and 0 <= int(action) < space.n
        )
    return action.shape == (space.dims,) and bool(
        np.all((action >= space.low) & (action <= space.high))
    )


def check_actions(spec: WorldSpec, active: Array, actions: Array) -> None:
    """`ActionError` for the first active agent whose action is outside `spec.action`."""
    if len(actions) != len(spec.agents):
        raise ValueError(f"expected {len(spec.agents)} action rows, got {len(actions)}")
    for agent, alive, action in zip(spec.agents, active, actions, strict=True):
        if alive and not _inside(spec.action, np.asarray(action)):
            raise ActionError(agent, np.asarray(action).tolist())


class ReplayWorld:
    """`core.World` double: every reset replays the recorded episode, whatever the seed."""

    def __init__(self, recording: WorldRecording) -> None:
        self.spec = recording.spec
        self.recording = recording
        self.seeds: list[int] = []
        self.actions: list[Array] = []
        self._taken: int | None = None

    def reset(self, seed: int) -> Step:
        self.seeds.append(seed)
        self._taken = 0
        return self.recording.start

    def step(self, actions: Array) -> Step:
        if self._taken is None:
            raise RuntimeError("step before reset")
        if self._taken == len(self.recording.steps):
            raise RuntimeError("step after the episode ended")
        current = self.recording.steps[self._taken - 1].step if self._taken else self.recording.start
        check_actions(self.spec, current.active, actions)
        self.actions.append(actions)
        self._taken += 1
        return self.recording.steps[self._taken - 1].step

    def result(self) -> EpisodeResult:
        if not self._taken:
            return self.recording.result
        return self.recording.steps[self._taken - 1].result

    def draw(self) -> DrawState:
        if not self._taken:
            return self.recording.draw
        return self.recording.steps[self._taken - 1].draw


class ReplayPolicy:
    """`core.Policy` (and `baselines.RulePolicy`) double: the recorded actions, in turn."""

    def __init__(self, recording: PolicyRecording) -> None:
        self.description = recording.description
        self.recording = recording
        self.seen: list[Array] = []

    def act(self, obs: Array, rng: np.random.Generator) -> Array:
        action = self.recording.actions[len(self.seen) % len(self.recording.actions)]
        self.seen.append(obs)
        return action


def fake_play_episode(
    world: World, policies: Mapping[str, Policy], seed: int, *, trace: bool = False
) -> Episode:
    """`core.play_episode` fake: the recorded rule-snake episode on seed 7."""
    episode = load_sample(Episode, "core.play_episode", "snake-rule-seed7")
    return episode if trace else replace(episode, frames=None)

"""`worlds.CheckWorld` replay double and the `worlds.make` fake, served from their recordings."""

from dataclasses import dataclass

from rllab.core import Array, World
from rllab.core.codec import load_sample
from rllab.core.doubles import ReplayWorld, WorldRecording


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CheckWorldRecording:
    """A recorded check-world episode plus the world's states and hand-derived best actions."""

    world: WorldRecording
    states: Array
    best_actions: Array


class ReplayCheckWorld(ReplayWorld):
    """`worlds.CheckWorld` double: a `ReplayWorld` that also states its answers."""

    def __init__(self, recording: CheckWorldRecording) -> None:
        super().__init__(recording.world)
        self.answers = recording

    def states(self) -> Array:
        return self.answers.states

    def best_actions(self) -> Array:
        return self.answers.best_actions


def fake_make(world: str, variant: str = "default", **overrides: int | float) -> World:
    """`worlds.make` fake: the seed-42 snake double, or a check-world double."""
    if overrides:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown override(s) {sorted(overrides)}")
    if variant != "default":
        raise ValueError(f"unknown variant {variant!r} of {world!r}")
    if world == "snake":
        return ReplayWorld(load_sample(WorldRecording, "worlds.make", "snake-seed42"))
    if world in {"check-discrete", "check-continuous"}:
        return ReplayCheckWorld(load_sample(CheckWorldRecording, "worlds.CheckWorld", world))
    raise ValueError(f"unknown world {world!r}")

"""Fakes of `baselines.rule_for` and `baselines.baseline_means`, served from their fixtures."""

from rllab.baselines.types import BaselineMeans, RulePolicy
from rllab.core.codec import load_sample
from rllab.core.doubles import PolicyRecording, ReplayPolicy


def fake_rule_for(world: str, variant: str, team: str) -> RulePolicy:
    """`baselines.rule_for` fake: the recorded snake rule double."""
    if (world, variant, team) != ("snake", "default", "snake"):
        raise KeyError(f"no rule for team {team!r} of {world!r} / {variant!r}")
    return ReplayPolicy(load_sample(PolicyRecording, "baselines.rule_for", "snake-rule"))


def fake_baseline_means(world: str, variant: str) -> BaselineMeans:
    """`baselines.baseline_means` fake: the snake `BaselineMeans`."""
    if (world, variant) != ("snake", "default"):
        raise KeyError(f"no rule for {world!r} / {variant!r}")
    return load_sample(BaselineMeans, "baselines.baseline_means", "snake")

"""Learner types: transitions, the `Learner` protocol and the methods' errors."""

from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

import numpy as np

from rllab.core import Array, Policy
from rllab.core.types import _fields_equal


@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class Transition:
    obs: Array
    actions: Array
    rewards: Array
    next_obs: Array
    done: bool
    truncated: bool
    active: Array

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        return _fields_equal(self, other)

    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        return hash((self.obs.shape, self.done, self.truncated))


class Learner(Protocol):
    def act(self, obs: Array, rng: np.random.Generator) -> Array: ...

    def observe(self, t: Transition) -> None: ...

    def policy(self) -> Policy: ...

    def state_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]: ...


class NonFiniteError(ArithmeticError):
    """A loss or parameter became NaN or infinite; raised before any parameter changes."""

    def __init__(self, value: float) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"non-finite value {value}")
        self.value = value


class SpecMismatchError(ValueError):
    """A checkpoint's world spec differs from the world it is loaded into."""

    def __init__(self, fields: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"checkpoint spec differs in {', '.join(fields)}")
        self.fields = tuple(fields)

"""`methods.Learner` replay double and the `make_learner` and `load_policy` fakes."""

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

from rllab.core import Array, MethodConfig, Policy, WorldSpec
from rllab.core.codec import load_sample
from rllab.core.doubles import PolicyRecording, ReplayPolicy
from rllab.methods.types import Learner, Transition
from rllab.runlog import Checkpoint


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LearnedStep:
    """One training step: the observation shown to `act`, its actions and the transition."""

    obs: Array
    actions: Array
    transition: Transition


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LearnerRecording:
    """A learner over a run of transitions, its frozen policy and its state dict."""

    steps: tuple[LearnedStep, ...]
    policy: PolicyRecording
    state: dict[str, object]


class ReplayLearner:
    """`methods.Learner` double: recorded actions in turn; keeps every transition it observes."""

    def __init__(self, recording: LearnerRecording) -> None:
        self.recording = recording
        self.seen: list[Array] = []
        self.observed: list[Transition] = []

    def act(self, obs: Array, rng: np.random.Generator) -> Array:
        step = self.recording.steps[len(self.seen) % len(self.recording.steps)]
        self.seen.append(obs)
        return step.actions

    def observe(self, t: Transition) -> None:
        self.observed.append(t)

    def policy(self) -> Policy:
        return ReplayPolicy(self.recording.policy)

    def state_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        return dict(self.recording.state)


def fake_make_learner(
    config: MethodConfig, spec: WorldSpec, team: str, rng: np.random.Generator
) -> Learner:
    """`methods.make_learner` fake: the recorded DQN learner double."""

"""Run-folder types: the run record, evaluation points, checkpoints, runs and progress."""

from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal, Protocol

from rllab.core import EpisodeResult, MethodConfig, RunConfig, WorldSpec


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Failure:
    step: int
    value: float
    checkpoint: Path


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunRecord:
    config: RunConfig
    spec: WorldSpec
    started: datetime
    ended: datetime | None
    status: Literal["running", "finished", "incomplete", "failed"]
    failure: Failure | None
    path: Path


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EvalPoint:
    step: int
    scores: Mapping[str, float]
    measures: Mapping[str, float]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Checkpoint:
    run: str
    pct: int
    step: int
    spec: WorldSpec
    methods: Mapping[str, MethodConfig]
    state: Mapping[str, dict[str, object]]
    path: Path


class Run(Protocol):
    record: RunRecord

    def episodes(self) -> list[EpisodeResult]: ...

    def evals(self) -> list[EvalPoint]: ...

    def checkpoints(self) -> list[Checkpoint]: ...


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Progress:
    step: int
    budget: int
    latest: EvalPoint | None
    elapsed: timedelta
    status: str


class RunExistsError(FileExistsError):
    """A run folder of that name already exists; nothing was written."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"run folder {path} already exists")
        self.path = path

"""`runlog.Run` and `runlog.RunWriter` replay doubles and the run-lookup fakes."""

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal, cast, get_args

from rllab.core import EpisodeResult, RunConfig, WorldSpec
from rllab.core.codec import load_sample
from rllab.runlog.types import Checkpoint, EvalPoint, Failure, Progress, Run, RunRecord

type Status = Literal["running", "finished", "incomplete", "failed"]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunRecording:
    """Everything one run folder holds: its record, logs and checkpoints."""

    record: RunRecord
    episodes: tuple[EpisodeResult, ...]
    evals: tuple[EvalPoint, ...]
    checkpoints: tuple[Checkpoint, ...]


class ReplayRun:
    """`runlog.Run` double: a recorded run folder, read-only."""

    def __init__(self, recording: RunRecording) -> None:
        self.record = recording.record
        self.recording = recording

    def episodes(self) -> list[EpisodeResult]:
        return list(self.recording.episodes)

    def evals(self) -> list[EvalPoint]:
        return list(self.recording.evals)

    def checkpoints(self) -> list[Checkpoint]:
        return list(self.recording.checkpoints)


class RecordingRunWriter:
    """`runlog.RunWriter` double: keeps every write in memory, touching no disk.

    `recording` holds the writes of a recorded 3-checkpoint snake run, to compare against; the
    record `close` returns takes its start and end times from it.
    """

    def __init__(self, root: Path, config: RunConfig, spec: WorldSpec) -> None:
        self.recording = load_sample(RunRecording, "runlog.RunWriter", "snake-3ckpt")
        self.folder = root / config.world / config.variant / config.name
        self.config = config
        self.spec = spec
        self.episodes: list[EpisodeResult] = []
        self.evals: list[EvalPoint] = []
        self.checkpoints: list[Checkpoint] = []
        self.closed: RunRecord | None = None

    def episode(self, result: EpisodeResult) -> None:
        self.episodes.append(result)

    def eval(self, point: EvalPoint) -> None:
        self.evals.append(point)

    def checkpoint(self, pct: int, step: int, state: Mapping[str, dict[str, object]]) -> Checkpoint:
        ckpt = Checkpoint(
            run=self.config.name,
            pct=pct,
            step=step,
            spec=self.spec,
            methods=self.config.methods,
            state=dict(state),
            path=self.folder / "checkpoints" / f"ckpt_{pct}.pt",
        )
        self.checkpoints.append(ckpt)
        return ckpt

    def close(self, status: str, failure: Failure | None = None) -> RunRecord:
        if status not in get_args(Status.__value__):
            raise ValueError(f"unknown run status {status!r}")
        self.closed = RunRecord(
            config=self.config,
            spec=self.spec,
            started=self.recording.record.started,
            ended=self.recording.record.ended,
            status=cast(Status, status),
            failure=failure,
            path=self.folder,
        )
        return self.closed


FIND_RUNS_CASES = tuple(f"snake-default-s{seed}" for seed in range(1, 7))


def fake_find_runs(
    root: Path, world: str, variant: str, *, include: Sequence[str] = ()
) -> list[Run]:
    """`runlog.find_runs` fake: 5 finished snake runs, plus the incomplete s6 when included."""
    if (world, variant) != ("snake", "default"):
        return []
    runs = [ReplayRun(load_sample(RunRecording, "runlog.find_runs", c)) for c in FIND_RUNS_CASES]
    return [r for r in runs if r.record.status == "finished" or r.record.config.name in include]


def fake_open_run(path: Path) -> Run:
    """`runlog.open_run` fake: the finished 3-checkpoint snake run double."""
    return ReplayRun(load_sample(RunRecording, "runlog.open_run", "snake-default-s1"))


def fake_progress(path: Path) -> Progress:
    """`runlog.progress` fake: a snake run at 35% with its 35% point written."""
    return load_sample(Progress, "runlog.progress", "snake-35pct")

"""Training types: the method check's result and its refusal."""

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CheckResult:
    method: str
    world: str
    agreement: float
    passed: bool


class CheckFailedError(RuntimeError):
    """A method failed its check world; no run was started."""

    def __init__(self, result: CheckResult) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            f"method {result.method!r} failed {result.world!r}: "
            f"agreement {result.agreement:.2f} < 0.95"
        )
        self.result = result

"""Fakes of the train contract functions, served from their fixtures.

`fake_run_train` stands in for PL-02 in PL-03 until the system task swaps in the real
`run_train`; it is module-level so `spawn` workers can import it.
"""

import json
from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from rllab.core import RunConfig
from rllab.core.codec import load_sample, to_json
from rllab.runlog import RunExistsError, RunRecord
from rllab.runlog.doubles import RunRecording
from rllab.train.types import CheckResult


def fake_load_run_configs(path: Path, seeds: Sequence[int]) -> list[RunConfig]:
    """`train.load_run_configs` fake: the recorded snake configs for seeds 1 and 2."""
    recorded = {
        config.seed: config
        for config in (
            load_sample(RunConfig, "train.load_run_configs", f"snake-default-s{seed}")
            for seed in (1, 2)
        )
    }
    missing = [seed for seed in seeds if seed not in recorded]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"no recorded config for seed(s) {missing}")
    return [recorded[seed] for seed in seeds]


def fake_run_check(config_path: Path, seed: int = 0) -> list[CheckResult]:
    """`train.run_check` fake: the passing DQN check."""
    return [load_sample(CheckResult, "train.run_check", "dqn-pass")]


def fake_run_train(config: RunConfig, root: Path) -> RunRecord:
    """`train.run_train` fake: writes the recorded finished 3-checkpoint snake run folder.

    The folder is `root/<world>/<variant>/<name>` with `config` in its record: `run.json`,
    `episodes.jsonl`, `evals.jsonl` and `checkpoints/ckpt_<pct>.pt` (a `torch.save` of the
    checkpoint's JSON form).
    """
    recording = load_sample(RunRecording, "train.run_train", "snake-default-s1")
    folder = root / config.world / config.variant / config.name
    if folder.exists():
        raise RunExistsError(folder)
    (folder / "checkpoints").mkdir(parents=True)
    record = replace(recording.record, config=config, path=folder)
    (folder / "run.json").write_text(json.dumps(to_json(record), indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    for name, rows in (("episodes", recording.episodes), ("evals", recording.evals)):
        lines = "".join(json.dumps(to_json(row)) + "\n" for row in rows)
        (folder / f"{name}.jsonl").write_text(lines, encoding="utf-8")
    for ckpt in recording.checkpoints:
        path = folder / "checkpoints" / f"ckpt_{ckpt.pct}.pt"
        torch.save(to_json(replace(ckpt, run=config.name, methods=config.methods, path=path)), path)
    return record


def fake_run_batch(
    config_path: Path,
    seeds: Sequence[int],
    root: Path,
    *,
    workers: int | None = None,
    check_seed: int = 0,
) -> list[RunRecord]:
    """`train.run_batch` fake: 2 finished snake records."""
    return [load_sample(RunRecord, "train.run_batch", f"snake-default-s{s}") for s in (1, 2)]

from collections.abc import Sequence


class MixedRunsError(ValueError):
    """The runs of one chart differ by more than their seed."""

    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"runs differ in {', '.join(names)}")

"""Fake of `charts.learning_curve`, served from its fixture."""

from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path

from rllab.baselines import BaselineMeans
from rllab.core import Output
from rllab.core.codec import CONTRACTS
from rllab.runlog import Run


def fake_learning_curve(
    runs: Sequence[Run], baselines: BaselineMeans, out: Path, *, measure: str | None = None
) -> Output:
    """`charts.learning_curve` fake: writes the placeholder PNG at `out`."""
    placeholder = CONTRACTS / "charts.learning_curve" / "placeholder.png"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_bytes(placeholder.read_bytes())
    return Output(path=out, kind="chart", made_from=tuple(r.record.config.name for r in runs))

"""Final-evaluation types: baseline comparisons, the verdict and the per-team summary."""

from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Comparison:
    baseline: Literal["random", "rule"]
    team: str
    learned_mean: float
    baseline_mean: float
    difference: float
    p_raw: float
    p_holm: float
    rejected: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Verdict:
    beats_baselines: bool
    failing_runs: tuple[str, ...]
    runs_needed: int

"""The `rllab` command: parse the arguments, call the pipeline entry, print its result (AD-10).

Each subcommand dispatches to its pipeline's entry; with `--smoke` it runs the pipeline's own
smoke inputs in a scratch folder instead. `cli` owns no pipeline step.
"""

import argparse
import sys
import tempfile
from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NoReturn

from rllab.cli.pipelines import pl04_watch, pl05_chart, pl06_evaluate
from rllab.train import run_batch, run_check
from rllab.train.pipelines import pl01_check, pl02_train, pl03_batch

RUNS = Path("runs")


class UsageError(ValueError):
    """A command line `rllab` can't parse."""


class _Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message: str) -> NoReturn:
        raise UsageError(message)


def parse_seeds(text: str) -> list[int]:
    """Seeds from `1-5`, `1,3,5` or a mix of the two."""
    seeds: list[int] = []
    for part in text.split(","):
        first, _, last = part.partition("-")
        seeds.extend(range(int(first), int(last or first) + 1))
    return seeds


def _check(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    return run_check(args.config, args.seed)


def _train(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    return run_batch(args.config, [args.seed], args.root)


def _batch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    seeds = parse_seeds(args.seeds)
    return run_batch(args.config, seeds, args.root, workers=args.workers, check_seed=args.seed)


def _watch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    return pl04_watch.run_watch(args.run_path)


def _chart(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    return pl05_chart.run_chart(
        args.root, args.world, args.variant, include=args.include, measure=args.measure
    )


def _evaluate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    return pl06_evaluate.run_evaluate(
        args.root, args.world, args.variant, include=args.include, workers=args.workers
    )


def _command(
    commands: "argparse._SubParsersAction[_Parser]",
    name: str,
    run: Callable[[argparse.Namespace], object],
    smoke: Callable[[Path], object],
    positionals: dict[str, type],
) -> _Parser:
    parser = commands.add_parser(name)
    for arg, kind in positionals.items():
        parser.add_argument(arg, nargs="?", type=kind)
    parser.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="run on the smoke inputs")
    parser.set_defaults(run=run, smoke_run=smoke, positionals=tuple(positionals))
    return parser


def build_parser() -> _Parser:
    """The `rllab` argument parser: `check`, `train`, `batch`, `watch`, `chart`, `evaluate`."""
    parser = _Parser(prog="rllab", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    check = _command(commands, "check", _check, pl01_check.smoke, {"config": Path})
    check.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    train = _command(commands, "train", _train, pl02_train.smoke, {"config": Path})
    train.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1)
    batch = _command(commands, "batch", _batch, pl03_batch.smoke, {"config": Path})
    batch.add_argument("--seeds", default="1-5")
    batch.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0, help="the method check's seed")
    _command(commands, "watch", _watch, pl04_watch.smoke, {"run_path": Path})
    chart = _command(commands, "chart", _chart, pl05_chart.smoke, {"world": str, "variant": str})
    chart.add_argument("--measure")
    world = {"world": str, "variant": str}
    evaluate = _command(commands, "evaluate", _evaluate, pl06_evaluate.smoke, world)
    for command in (train, batch, chart, evaluate):
        command.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=RUNS)
    for command in (chart, evaluate):
        command.add_argument("--include", action="append", default=[])
    for command in (batch, evaluate):
        command.add_argument("--workers", type=int)
    return parser


def _dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rllab-smoke-") as work:
            return args.smoke_run(Path(work))
    missing = [name for name in args.positionals if getattr(args, name) is None]
    if missing:
        raise UsageError(f"{args.command}: missing {', '.join(missing)}")
    return args.run(args)


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run one `rllab` command; every error is one line on stderr and exit code 1."""
    try:
        result = _dispatch(build_parser().parse_args(argv))
    except Exception as exc:  # the command's one error line, whatever failed
        print(f"rllab: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for item in result if isinstance(result, list) else [result]:
        print(item)
    return 0

"""Generate tests/contracts/<symbol>/ samples and schemas for M1-T01 (scratch, not committed)."""

import json
import sys
import types
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import MISSING, fields, is_dataclass, replace
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal, TypeAliasType, Union, get_args, get_origin, get_type_hints

import numpy as np

from rllab.baselines import BaselineMeans
from rllab.core import (
    ActionSpace,
    Box,
    Discrete,
    Drawable,
    DrawState,
    Episode,
    EpisodeResult,
    Frame,
    MeasureSpec,
    MethodConfig,
    Output,
    RunConfig,
    Step,
    TeamSpec,
    WorldSpec,
)
from rllab.core.codec import to_json
from rllab.core.doubles import PolicyRecording, RecordedStep, WorldRecording
from rllab.evaluate import Comparison, Summary, Verdict
from rllab.methods import Transition
from rllab.methods.doubles import LearnedStep, LearnerRecording
from rllab.runlog import Checkpoint, EvalPoint, Failure, Progress, RunRecord
from rllab.runlog.doubles import RunRecording
from rllab.train import CheckResult
from rllab.worlds.doubles import CheckWorldRecording

ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1]) / "tests" / "contracts"
F32 = np.float32


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- schema
def schema_of(tp: Any, defs: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if isinstance(tp, TypeAliasType):
        return schema_of(tp.__value__, defs)
    origin = get_origin(tp) or tp
    args = get_args(tp)
    if tp in (Any, object):
        return {}
    if tp is type(None):
        return {"type": "null"}
    if origin is Literal:
        return {"enum": list(args)}
    if origin in (Union, types.UnionType):
        return {"anyOf": [schema_of(a, defs) for a in args]}
    if origin is tuple:
        if len(args) == 2 and args[1] is Ellipsis:
            return {"type": "array", "items": schema_of(args[0], defs)}
        return {
            "type": "array",
            "prefixItems": [schema_of(a, defs) for a in args],
            "items": False,
            "minItems": len(args),
            "maxItems": len(args),
        }
    if origin in (list, Sequence):
        return {"type": "array", "items": schema_of(args[0], defs) if args else {}}
    if origin in (dict, Mapping):
        return {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": schema_of(args[1], defs)}
    if origin is np.ndarray:
        defs["Array"] = {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "dtype": {"enum": ["float32", "float64", "int64", "bool"]},
                "shape": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0}},
                "data": {},
            },
            "required": ["dtype", "shape", "data"],
            "additionalProperties": False,
        }
        return {"$ref": "#/$defs/Array"}
    if is_dataclass(origin):
        name = origin.__name__
        if name not in defs:
            defs[name] = {}
            hints = get_type_hints(origin)
            defs[name] = {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {f.name: schema_of(hints[f.name], defs) for f in fields(origin)},
                "required": [f.name for f in fields(origin) if f.default is MISSING],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            }
        return {"$ref": f"#/$defs/{name}"}
    simple = {
        bool: {"type": "boolean"},
        int: {"type": "integer"},
        float: {"type": "number"},
        str: {"type": "string"},
        Path: {"type": "string"},
        datetime: {"type": "string", "format": "date-time"},
        timedelta: {"type": "number", "minimum": 0},
    }
    return simple[tp]


def write_folder(symbol: str, tp: Any, samples: dict[str, Any], schema: dict | None = None) -> None:
    folder = ROOT / symbol
    (folder / "samples").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if schema is None:
        defs: dict[str, Any] = {}
        body = schema_of(tp, defs)
        schema = {"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema", "title": symbol}
        schema.update(body)
        if defs:
            schema["$defs"] = dict(sorted(defs.items()))
    (folder / "schema.json").write_text(json.dumps(schema, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    for case, value in samples.items():
        text = json.dumps(to_json(value), indent=1) + "\n"
        (folder / "samples" / f"{case}.json").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ snake
HEADINGS = [(0, -1), (1, 0), (0, 1), (-1, 0)]  # up, right, down, left (y grows downward)
SNAKE_SPEC = WorldSpec(
    world="snake",
    variant="default",
    agents=("snake",),
    teams=(TeamSpec("snake", (0,), "food eaten", "higher"),),
    obs_len=12,
    action=Discrete(3),
    max_steps=1000,
    measures=(MeasureSpec("length at death", "snake", "higher"),),
    sight=None,
)


class MiniSnake:
    """A tiny snake for realistic recordings: actions 0 left, 1 straight, 2 right."""

    def __init__(self, seed: int) -> None:
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        self.seed = seed
        self.body = [(4, 4), (4, 5), (4, 6)]
        self.heading = 0
        self.food = self.place()
        self.eaten = 0
        self.total = 0.0
        self.steps = 0
        self.hungry = 0
        self.done = False

    def place(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        free = [(x, y) for x in range(10) for y in range(10) if (x, y) not in self.body]
        return free[int(self.rng.integers(len(free)))]

    def fatal(self, cell: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
        x, y = cell
        return not (0 <= x < 10 and 0 <= y < 10) or cell in self.body[:-1]

    def ahead(self, action: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
        h = (self.heading + action - 1) % 4
        dx, dy = HEADINGS[h]
        return (self.body[0][0] + dx, self.body[0][1] + dy)

    def obs(self) -> np.ndarray:
        hx, hy = self.body[0]
        fx, fy = self.food
        row = [float(self.fatal(self.ahead(a))) for a in (1, 0, 2)]
        row += [float(self.heading == h) for h in range(4)]
        row += [float(fy < hy), float(fx > hx), float(fy > hy), float(fx < hx)]
        row += [float(len(self.body))]
        return np.asarray([row], dtype=F32)

    def step(self, action: int) -> tuple[float, bool, bool]:
        self.heading = (self.heading + action - 1) % 4
        dx, dy = HEADINGS[self.heading]
        head = (self.body[0][0] + dx, self.body[0][1] + dy)
        self.steps += 1
        self.hungry += 1
        if self.fatal(head):
            self.done = True
            reward = -1.0
        elif head == self.food:
            self.body.insert(0, head)
            self.eaten += 1
            self.hungry = 0
            self.food = self.place()
            reward = 1.0
        else:
            self.body.insert(0, head)
            self.body.pop()
            reward = 0.0
        if self.hungry >= 100:
            self.done = True
        truncated = not self.done and self.steps >= SNAKE_SPEC.max_steps
        self.done = self.done or truncated
        self.total += reward
        return reward, self.done, truncated

    def draw(self) -> DrawState:
        objs = [Drawable("snake-head", float(self.body[0][0]), float(self.body[0][1]), 1.0, "snake", 0)]
        objs += [Drawable("snake-body", float(x), float(y), 1.0, "snake", 0) for x, y in self.body[1:]]
        objs.append(Drawable("food", float(self.food[0]), float(self.food[1]), 1.0, None, None))
        return DrawState(10.0, 10.0, tuple(objs))

    def result(self) -> EpisodeResult:
        return EpisodeResult(
            seed=self.seed,
            length=self.steps,
            scores={"snake": float(self.eaten)},
            team_rewards={"snake": self.total},
            measures={"length at death": float(len(self.body))},
        )

    def rule(self) -> int:
        hx, hy = self.body[0]
        fx, fy = self.food
        dx, dy = fx - hx, fy - hy
        if dx == 0 or (dy != 0 and abs(dy) < abs(dx)):
            want = 0 if dy < 0 else 2
        else:
            want = 1 if dx > 0 else 3
        turn = (want - self.heading) % 4
        preferred = {0: 1, 1: 2, 3: 0, 2: 2}[turn]
        options = [preferred] + [a for a in (1, 0, 2) if a != preferred]
        return next((a for a in options if not self.fatal(self.ahead(a))), preferred)


def step_of(obs: np.ndarray, reward: float, done: bool, truncated: bool) -> Step:
    return Step(
        obs=obs,
        rewards=np.asarray([reward], dtype=F32),
        active=np.asarray([True]),
        done=done,
        truncated=truncated,
    )


def record_snake(seed: int, policy: Any) -> tuple[WorldRecording, list[Frame], list[int]]:
    s = MiniSnake(seed)
    start = step_of(s.obs(), 0.0, False, False)
    draw0, result0 = s.draw(), s.result()
    frames = [Frame(0, draw0, {"snake": 0.0}, np.asarray([0.0], dtype=F32))]
    steps, actions = [], []
    while not s.done:
        a = policy(s)
        actions.append(a)
        reward, done, truncated = s.step(a)
        st = step_of(s.obs(), reward, done, truncated)
        steps.append(RecordedStep(np.asarray([a], dtype=np.int64), st, s.draw(), s.result()))
        frames.append(Frame(s.steps, s.draw(), {"snake": float(s.eaten)}, st.rewards))
    rec = WorldRecording(SNAKE_SPEC, seed, start, draw0, result0, tuple(steps))
    return rec, frames, actions
